newsitem.title: MALI: Mali confirms Konare election win, turnout low.
newsitem.headline: Mali confirms Konare election win, turnout low.

text.p: Official results of Mali's May 11 presidential election, which was boycotted by main opposition parties, show President Alpha Oumar Konare re-elected with 84.36 percent of votes, the electoral commission said on Saturday.
It put turnout at 28 percent of the 5.4 million electorate. Konare's challenger, businessman Mamadou Maribatrou Diaby polled just 45,160 votes.
Opposition parties declined to put up a candidate in protest over the chaotic April parliamentary election which was annulled by the constitutional court and will be rerun in July.
The opposition is still demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Ibrahim Keita and the dissolution of the electoral commission.

Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system. Military leader Amadou Toumani Toure stepped down after 14 months and now often mediates in regional political crises.
